html:
SMTO-ART-0009 — SMTO can't add new files to this Task anymore

GUID: db3cc11a-982d-47b5-9363-1f1420438ebf
Slug: artifact-permission-denied
Domain: ART · Subsystem: art

What happened

  • SMTO tried to save a new file from this Task, but the Task's files were deleted, are being checked by a cleanup, or its conversation was removed. The new file wasn't added.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Artifacts from this run for the Task. If it says the files from this run have been deleted, they were removed by Delete artifacts, Delete everything or an age limit. Once a Task's files are deleted, SMTO won't add new ones to it, so the deletion stays complete.
  2. If the files are still listed, wait a minute, then select Retry collection if it appears. The hourly cleanup only blocks new files while it is checking that Task.
  3. If the files were deleted, ask SMTO in a new message to create the file again. A new Task has its own place to keep files, so the new copy can be saved.

What success looks like

  • The file appears in Artifacts from this run for the Task that made it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't change folder permissions or delete files on the server to force the save; that can undo a deletion someone asked for.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Artifact publication was refused because the run's workspace is absent, retired, tombstoned, owned by another conversation, or held by an active maintenance cleanup claim.

What this means

  • Publication finds the run namespace absent, retired, tombstoned, wrong-conversation or under an active cleanup claim. Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.

Why this can happen

  • Publication finds the run namespace absent, retired, tombstoned, wrong-conversation or under an active cleanup claim.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect namespace ownership and cleanup/deletion state; this producer does not establish an OS permission failure.

How to fix it

  • Inspect artifact_workspaces (retired, conversation_id), native tombstones and artifact_cleanup_claims for the run. If retirement or deletion was intended, publish from a new run; if only a cleanup claim was held, retry collection after the maintenance pass releases it. Never change filesystem permissions or remove registry rows to get past this check.
  • Reconcile workspace ownership and cleanup/deletion state through supported controls before publishing; do not change filesystem permissions to bypass a lifecycle fence.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported active owned workspace admits publication after its actual lifecycle conflict is resolved.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass workspace ownership, cleanup claims or retired-workspace fences by editing permissions or deleting evidence.

Technical notes

  • Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
